Bain Capital Private Equity's own portfolio list carries it ('Shopping.com (Formerly Dealtime.com)'), beside the generalist-fund names (Staples, Bright Horizons, DoubleClick, Ameritrade), while the venture funds' positions of the same years (Taleo, Vonage, Tengion, aPriori) are absent from it; the firm never listed it on its live 2007-vintage list, and no filing or release read names a Bain Capital venture vehicle as a holder.

The firm's 2006 rendering 'Stream International', the same company as the row 'stream' (identity-merges.json), which is ruled out; the ruling is the same: [bain_capital_heritage] Another desk (decisions.md D1, D2, R1): Stream International (technical-support outsourcing, Richardson, TX), 'acquired by Solectron (NYSE: SLR) in October 2001' (the firm's 2012 page), listed by the firm only in 2006-2013 under 'Expansion/Growth Buyout'; the private-equity list carries 'Stream'. This replaces its earlier classification as a member. The Princeton Review, the same company as the row 'education-holdings-1-the-princeton-review' (identity-merges.json), which is ruled out; the ruling is the same: The Princeton Review was listed on NASDAQ (REVU) from its 2001 IPO (the firm's own archive: 'IPO on 6/19/01'); BCV's 2007 investment was preferred stock issued by the listed company (its 8-K of 2007-07-26 defines the 'Bain Fund'), later renamed Education Holdings 1. A placement into a public company is not a venture round (COLLECTION.md s1 T3; decisions.md D4).

The firm's 2006 rendering 'Interpath / USInternetworking', the same company as the row 'usinternetworking' (identity-merges.json), which is ruled out; the ruling is the same: USinternetworking (the row absorbs the 2006 listing 'Interpath / USInternetworking', Expansion/Growth Buyout): USi, listed on NASDAQ since its 1999 IPO, filed a prepackaged Chapter 11 in January 2002 under which 'USi Holdings, an investment affiliate of Bain Capital Partners, LLC, will invest up to $106 million in USi' and 'When completed, Bain will own all of the equity in USi' (USi's 8-K press release, 2002-01-07); it emerged in May 2002 merged with Interpath (Wikipedia). A 100% acquisition by a Bain Capital private-equity affiliate of a listed company is neither a venture round nor a BCV desk position (COLLECTION.md s1 T3 control positions; decisions.md D1, D4). AT&T bought it in 2006.

A position of Bain Capital's generalist funds (Bain Capital Fund I onward, today the private-equity family under CRD 145652's sister adviser CRD 145653), made before any Bain Capital venture vehicle existed; the firm's own 2006 page files these deals under 'Bain Capital's history of investing ... since 1984' and dates BCV itself to 2001.

(Wellesley, MA), the Form D-only row of a 2009 $185M offering naming a 'Jeffrey Schwartz' as director: a company listed on NYSE Amex since its 2008 formation (the former Global BPO Services Corp.), so the filing is a placement into a listed company, not a venture round (COLLECTION.md s1 T3); nothing ties it to a BCV fund, and it is not the Stream International the firm listed (ruled on its own row).
